Artist Casey Curran creates kinetic sculptures that combine mechanical systems with forms inspired by plants and natural structures. In this prototype, layers of delicate petals are connected so that a single mechanical action produces a rippling movement across the entire structure. Instead of every element moving independently, the motion travels through the sculpture like a wave. This type of movement is central to Curran’s practice. Using motors, wires, cranks and carefully engineered mechanisms, he creates artificial flowers and organisms that bloom, flutter and contract.  The machinery is artificial, but the movement feels strangely organic ,engineering becomes a way of imitating the rhythms of living systems. #art #artist #fashion #avantgarde #design

Janel Hawkins, founder of Sand Castle University, transforms compacted sand into detailed sculptures, from elaborate castles to animals and imaginative characters. Kinetic sculptor Reuben Margolin  creates intricate mechanical installations inspired by mathematics, natural movement, and wave phenomena. Cadence (2024) is a suspended sculpture measuring approximately 3.35 meters in diameter. A single electric motor controls 216 strings connected to an articulated hexagonal lattice made from tapered maple dowels. As the strings move, the wooden structure produces continuous, fluid waves, resembling the movement of water. His Caterpillar Clock (2026) explores a different form of mechanical motion. Built from polished brass, its precisely counterbalanced mechanism uses a small electric motor to move around a large gear, completing one revolution every six minutes. #art #artist #niche #sculpture #design
